newsitem.title: USA: CBS TV station revs turnaround seen in Q3.
newsitem.headline: CBS TV station revs turnaround seen in Q3.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp director and senior executive Mel Karmazin said Wednesday he expects a turnaround in revenues for CBS's television station operation as soon as the third quarter.
"You will see as soon as the third quarter a turnaround in the big markets ... in the top line," Karmazin said in an address at a Montgomery Securities conference here.
CBS is a unit of Westinghouse.

Karmazin, chairman of the CBS radio unit, was recently named head of its TV stations group as well. Referring to the TV group's underperformance, he said there would be "no excuses" about lack of revenue growth.
He said both the TV and radio operations had "tremendous" growth potential and that recent "progress" had been extraordinary.
He said part of the problem with the TV station group stemmed from a sales force on its owned and operated stations that derived 75 percent of its pay from salary and 25 percent from commissions.
He said that beginning July 1, all sales sfaff will be paid straight commission, which he expects will motivate sales executives to boost ad revenues.
CBS owns TV stations in seven of the top 10 U.S. markets and reaches 32 percent of U.S. households.
Last month Karmazin, a big CBS shareholder, took the reins of the TV operation from Peter Lund.

Karmazin said the CBS radio business continued to provide healthy cash flow, citing Montgomery's estimates of $600-$700 million expected to be generated in 1998. Without agreeing with the estimates, Karmazin said he expected the radio business to generate "a tremendous amount of free cash flow."
He said the company would not use more than two percent of the cash flow for capital expenditures, which will allow it to buy other television stations and also buy back Westinghouse stock.
Karmazin referred to Westinghouse as a "large-cap growth company that throws off (a great amount of) free cash flow."
